My dear [Florence](../persons.html#1520),
In the first place my [Incurable](../others.html#37) Vote is promised two deep so I am afraid that is of no use.
I could not answer before as I was at the [G F S](../others.html#23) annual Conference - more over my [colleague](../persons.html#329) took the M S away to read.

She approves of it much, and we hope to put it in among the short stories, when we can.[^1] The same may be said of [Emma](../persons.html#1519)’s poem, but I don’t know how to fix any time.[^2] I have more to do than I can do today and it is almost Church time, so good bye
Your affectionate

C M Yonge
Can you get any [Mother’s](../others.html#31) ladies to order this

[^1]: Perhaps the MS was \'Limp Ladies\', MP (August 1891), 186-168, which was the next article signed by Wilford to appear in the magazine.

[^2]: Her correspondent’s sister Emma Wilford (b. 1832/3). A poem ‘The Treasures of the Snow: Feast of the Purification’, signed ‘W.’ appeared in MP (February 1891). (The feast of the Purification is 2 February.)
